hints: Focus on what type of compound actually reacts with HCN to make a cyanohydrin, and what the new carbon will be bonded to.
Remember HCN adds across C=O to give $\text{C(OH)(CN)}$, so draw the product from ethanal as $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ and list its four groups.
Check which product carbon ends up with four different groups, remembering that two identical ethyl groups or two H atoms can never be chiral.
walkthrough:
**Recall HCN addition**

Aldehydes and ketones undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN to form hydroxynitriles called cyanohydrins. Esters do not react this way.

General equation:
$$\text{R}_2\text{C=O} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{R}_2\text{C(OH)CN}$$

**Recall what makes a chiral centre**

A chiral carbon must have four different atoms or groups attached to it. If any two groups are the same, it cannot be chiral.

**Test each carbonyl compound**

For $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO}$ the product is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$. The central carbon has $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$, all different, so it is chiral.

For $\text{HCHO}$ the product is $\text{CH}_2\text{(OH)CN}$, with two $\text{H}$ atoms, so achiral. For $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ the product has two identical $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ groups, so achiral.

**Conclude the answer**

Only ethanal gives a cyanohydrin with four different groups on the new carbon. That is the compound that creates a chiral centre.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CN}$ (2-hydroxypropanenitrile). The C-2 is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{CH}_3$, $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$, four different groups, so it is a chiral centre. A racemic mixture is formed.
options.B: Incorrect. Pentan-3-one, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, does form a cyanohydrin, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{C(OH)(CN)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$, but the central carbon has two identical ethyl groups. With only three distinct groups it is achiral.
options.C: Incorrect. Methyl ethanoate, $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{CH}_3$, is an ester, not an aldehyde or ketone. It does not undergo nucleophilic addition with HCN to give a cyanohydrin under these conditions.
options.D: Incorrect. Methanal, $\text{HCHO}$, does react: $\text{HCHO} + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{HOCH}_2\text{CN}$. The product carbon is bonded to two H atoms plus $\text{OH}$ and $\text{CN}$, so it has only three distinct groups and is not chiral.
